summary_en: Which inter-firm relationships persist over time and which disappear? Lőrincz analyses a population-scale network of Hungarian business-to-business transactions and ownership ties and finds that transaction relationships are persistent in a structured way: they cluster geographically, run within rather than across industries, and are reinforced by ownership ties between buyer and seller. The paper documents the link structure of the Hungarian inter-firm economy and provides a baseline for later work on contagion, supply-chain disruptions, and policy targeting.
data_used: Population-scale Hungarian business-to-business transaction data (likely NAV invoice / VAT-control records) combined with firm-ownership records, used to construct a longitudinal inter-firm network. Analysis at the firm-pair level over multiple years.
policy_relevance: Foundational for Hungarian economic-policy questions where inter-firm structure matters: supply-chain resilience after shocks (energy-price spike, Russia-Ukraine disruption), targeted SME finance via bank loan guarantees, monitoring tax-evasion networks (NAV operations), and competition-policy assessment of vertical relationships. Provides the empirical map a Hungarian policymaker needs to reason quantitatively about contagion in real-world inter-firm linkages.
title: Business transactions and ownership ties between firms
